Answer submitted by the executor: The C-H bond in acetylenes is more reactive than in typical hydrocarbons primarily because terminal acetylenic hydrogens are more acidic. This increased acidity is due to the sp-hybridization of the carbon atom in the acetylene, which gives the carbon greater s-character (50%) compared to sp² or sp³ hybridized carbons in other hydrocarbons. The greater s-character pulls electron density closer to the carbon nucleus, making the C-H bond more polarized and the hydrogen more easily removed as a proton..
